part: problem scope and knock-on analysis for the Georgia Tech 2021 page

denominators.note: Scope is measured against the source dataset: 22 participants in the original study, of which 16 are here (2,301 recordings) and six are not converted (846 recordings in the authors' 2024 copy). A step is one heel strike to the next heel strike of one leg; the 16 local participants have 78,604 of them in the source gait tables (21,363,858 samples). Only 102 recordings (1,299 steps), all from AB06, have been rebuilt, so measured counts below come from small checked sets and say so. Sample counts are given only where an audit has them.

problems.card: Force plates and force signs were picked from force and ankle-moment waveforms

status.label: Fixed in a checked pilot
status.detail: New rules ran in small trial runs (a pilot) and agree with the source. The full rebuild has not adopted them.

problems.wrong: For overground walking the old conversion code decided which plate belonged to which foot with early-stance and late-swing force thresholds, and it chose the sign of forward force and centre of pressure by whichever matched the ankle moment curve. That can put one foot's force on the other foot or flip a sign without the data saying so.
problems.how: The code review found both rules. Plate positions and pelvis markers can answer the same questions without the moment curve. Treadmill plates are named by side, and the one treadmill pilot recording shows one sign matching the measured plate data to rounding error.
problems.example: One of 24 legs drawn at random from the 228 legs of the treadmill pilot recording (seed 20261118): a left leg where assuming forward force is positive is off by up to 0.13 body weights and assuming it is negative is off by only 5e-15.
problems.total_line: In the 36 recordings compared before and after (30 overground, 6 treadmill, all AB06; 128,400 rows) the new rules changed 484,957 force values. None of the other columns changed.
problems.denominator_text: Of the 2,301 local recordings, 36 have been compared before and after, all from AB06, so 1.6% of recordings. Percentages are not extrapolated. The old rule applied to every recording with force plates. Overground values changed from missing to measured; treadmill values changed from measured to missing, mostly because centre of pressure is now left missing when the foot carries under 0.2 body weight.
problems.grid_caption: Share of each group's recordings that the new rules were compared on. Zero means not looked at.
problems.figure_question: Which participants and tasks have been compared before and after?
problems.direction: Direction: a wrong plate or sign changes force and centre of pressure. Angles and the authors' joint moments are separate source columns.

problems.card: Sideways force and centre of pressure point opposite ways for the two feet

status.label: Decided by José, fix not yet run
status.detail: José chose option B: positive outward for each leg, so the left leg is mirrored. The conversion code has not been changed or run for this.

problems.wrong: The sideways columns were exported on the lab's fixed X axis. That axis points to the person's right when they face the lab's negative Z direction. So it points outward for the right foot and inward for the left foot, and it flips when they walk the other way. The name 'lateral' therefore does not describe the numbers.
problems.how: We read the force plate table of three treadmill recordings drawn at random (seed 20261118), one at a time. On the right plate the mean sideways force over stance is -32.1, -23.1 and -27.4 N; on the left plate it is +31.8, +40.9 and +23.4 N. Same axis, opposite signs.
problems.example: AB07, treadmill trial 2: 123 right-foot and 123 left-foot stance phases averaged. The right foot pushes toward negative X, the left toward positive X.
problems.total_line: All 2,301 local recordings (100%), in the two sideways force columns and the two sideways centre-of-pressure columns, wherever a plate gives a value.
problems.denominator_text: Recordings: 2,301 local ones; the 846 not yet converted would be affected the same way. Steps and samples are not counted because the fix is not run. In 8 recordings checked for walking direction, 72,143 of 76,909 on-plate samples (93.8%) face -Z, 4,486 (5.8%) face +Z and 280 (0.4%) walk along X.
problems.grid_caption: Every recording carries the sideways columns, so every cell is affected.

problems.direction: Direction: the sign fix changes only sideways force and sideways centre of pressure. It does not reach vertical or forward values or any angle.

problems.card: Pelvis tilt, and the angles built on it, do not match the markers

status.label: Decided by José, fix not yet run
status.detail: José chose option C: take tilt from the pelvis markers directly. The conversion code has not been changed or run for this.

problems.wrong: The old conversion code exported the authors' model 'pelvis tilt' as forward-back tilt. The authors' model turns the pelvis about 90 degrees in heading, so that column is not forward-back tilt. After removing the heading, no tilt we can derive from the authors' data follows the marker tilt over treadmill strides, and overground it follows only partly. Thigh, shank, foot and trunk angles were built on that tilt.
problems.how: We compared each candidate with the tilt of the four pelvis markers over the strides of 8 recordings drawn at random (seed 20261027). Stride-average agreement on the two treadmill recordings is 0.07 and -0.25 (1 would be identical). In a separate set of 131 recordings, only 1 had the model's heading in the forward-back frame.
problems.example: AB08 treadmill, 124 strides: the published pelvis tilt agrees with the marker tilt at 0.03. The marker-based tilt sits about 19 degrees from the model's zero.
problems.total_line: The pelvis tilt column and four angle columns built on it (thigh, shank, foot, trunk) in all 2,301 local recordings (100%).
problems.denominator_text: Recordings: 2,301 local ones. Evidence comes from 8 recordings (7 participants) for agreement and 131 recordings (6 participants) for heading. Strides and samples are not counted for the whole set.

problems.card: Joint-angle zero is now defined by the segment angles

status.label: Decided by José, fix not yet run
status.detail: José decided on 23 November 2026: joint angles are differences of segment angles, and segment angles are measured against gravity, so there is no separate joint zero (no static pose, no model zero). The conversion code has not been changed or run for this.
status.needs: Needs segment angles (thigh, shank, foot and pelvis) for every recording. Pelvis-marker tilt is available (the earlier pelvis decision); whether thigh, shank and foot angles can be built from the markers and the ankle centre found: not checked. A guarded job is needed to measure how far the old zeros differ from the new one.

problems.wrong: Joint angles come in two versions. One is zero at the model's own zero. The other is the trial angle minus the average of the participant's static standing trial (added by the authors in April 2024). The conversion code reads the relative version, our sign tests used the model zero, and the 2021 archive of AB17 has no relative version. José has now decided the zero (see the status above); the size of the difference between the old files and the new rule is not measured.
problems.how: The README dates the relative files to 28 April 2024, and the authors' script subtracts the column average of the first static trial it finds, without wrapping angles. We then tried to measure the difference with our safe file reader: it refused all 20 files we tried (16 static-pose files and one relative file for each of the four tasks).
problems.example: No measured example exists: the size of the difference has not been measured, so the figure is a made-up illustration, labelled as one.
problems.total_line: Every joint angle in all 2,301 local recordings (100%) is affected by the new zero rule. The size of the difference is not measured.

problems.card: Forward force and centre of pressure use one fixed lab direction

status.label: Documented only, kept as published
status.detail: Forward values are measured on the lab Z axis only. They are kept with this limit stated.

problems.wrong: Forward force and forward centre of pressure use the lab Z axis, signed by the measured pelvis direction of each step. A step is kept while the walking path stays within 45 degrees of Z. On curved overground paths the forward value is therefore under-reported. Steps where the direction is unclear are left missing.
problems.how: We measured the path direction in 8 recordings drawn at random (seed 20261027). The 95th percentile of the deviation from Z is 7.7 to 36.4 degrees, lowest on the treadmill and highest overground.
problems.example: AB16 level walking: half of the samples deviate by 5.2 degrees or less, 95% by 36.4 degrees or less, and the worst by 45.0.

problems.card: Centre of pressure is measured from the outer ankle marker, not from the decided origin

status.label: Decided by José, fix not yet run
status.detail: José decided on 23 November 2026: the centre of pressure moves with the foot, with its origin 100 mm forward of the ankle joint centre along the foot's heel-to-toe direction. The conversion code has not been changed or run for this.
status.needs: Needs the ankle joint centre and the foot's direction for every sample, from markers. Whether the markers give them: not checked. The current offset from the outer ankle marker is not measured.

problems.wrong: Centre of pressure is stored relative to the outer ankle marker, not the ankle joint centre. The distance between the two is not measured. The authors' own centre of pressure is also filtered at 15 Hz by default, and is set to the plate origin when the plate sees almost no load; our code leaves those samples missing.
problems.how: The authors' scripts were read line by line. In 8 sampled recordings the centre of pressure lies a median of 9.4 cm from the nearer foot, so it lands near the foot.
problems.example: A median distance of 9.4 cm to the nearer foot says the values land near the right foot. It does not say how far they sit from the ankle joint.
problems.total_line: All centre-of-pressure columns in all 2,301 local recordings (100%) are relative to the ankle marker, not to the decided origin (100 mm forward of the ankle joint centre in the foot's frame). The offset to the joint is not measured.

checked_fine: All 4,602 source gait-phase tables of the 16 local participants were read: 21,363,858 samples, 0 non-finite or out of range, and 0 of 78,604 steps with a timing problem.
All 1,680 local ramp and stair recordings carry a terrain label and a positive incline or stair height.
Force values of 51 completed recordings (1,111 steps) match the original force and marker tables; the largest difference is 2e-12.
The sign test on 648 leg channels (6 participants, seeded) found 0 wrong signs; 127 channels were left undecided and are not counted as passed.
Vertical force and centre-of-pressure height use the lab's up axis; the lab frame was right-handed in all 8 sampled recordings.
other_limits: Plate moments are not exported: their reference point and sign are not stated, and values of hundreds of newton-metres on contact show they are not free moments.
Overground files include a virtual 'Combined' plate (a force-weighted merge of the real plates) that we do not separate from its parts.
Static-pose file choice in the authors' script depends on file ordering, so the intended calibration for a participant is unknown.
The 2024 source folder is a live working copy: one file in AB28 is dated October 2026, so each download re-lists the folder first.
No producer log ties the shipped force-conversion tools to the published force files; the frame is corroborated by data, not proven by the producer.
